Asset Based Lending Announces Fourth Securitization of $200 Million, Marking Largest Transaction to Date
News provided by
Asset Based Lending, LLC
Nov 12, 2026, 13:33 ET
Share this article
Share this article
JERSEY CITY, N.J. , Nov. 12, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Asset Based Lending (ABL) , a national private lender and a driving force behind the next generation of real estate investment, has successfully closed its fourth unrated securitization, totaling $200 million. The transaction, ABL 2026 RTL-1, which priced on October 15 and closed on October 26, marks ABL's largest to date, bringing its cumulative securitization volume to $723 million.
The transaction is backed by a diversified pool of business-purpose residential real estate loans, with an industry-leading concentration of ground-up infill construction loans. This reflects ABL's 16 years of experience in ground-up construction lending and its proven ability to manage the complexities and risks of residential development.
"We are proud to lead the industry in financing ground-up construction, and to do it at a cost that keeps our pricing competitive for the builders we serve," said Kevin Rodman, CEO of ABL. "This transaction underscores the strength of the platform our team has built and the confidence investors have in our credit. Every one of these loans puts new housing on the ground."
The transaction also demonstrates ABL's ability to navigate challenging market conditions. Despite heightened volatility and increased investor selectivity across the securitization market, ABL secured competitive financing terms. The deal reached the market in approximately three weeks, making it one of the company's fastest securitization executions.
Performance Trust Capital Partners, LLC served as structuring agent, with Nomura Securities International, Inc. ("Nomura") and Mizuho Securities USA LLC serving as joint bookrunners.
"Successfully executing this transaction amid market volatility reinforces the effectiveness of our capital markets strategy and the quality of our platform," said Daniel Gotay, Head of Capital Markets at ABL. "We have built durable relationships with institutional investors and established a track record they can underwrite, giving us consistent access to capital. For our borrowers, that is what matters most: they can count on ABL to fund their projects from start to finish."
The securitization also reflects ABL's expanding national footprint, with collateral spanning the Northeast, Sun Belt, Rust Belt and South. This geographic diversification supports the company's strategy to continue growing beyond its established Northeast presence and finance residential development in markets across the country.
To learn more about ABL, please visit www.ablfunding.com .
About Asset Based Lending
Asset Based Lending was established in 2010, providing fast bridge financing to real estate investors for the purchase, renovation, new construction, and long-term refinance of single-family, multi-family, and mixed-use properties. A trusted lender to thousands of investors, Asset Based Lending has closed over $4.4 billion in loans since its founding. Learn more at https://www.ablfunding.com/ . Follow the company on LinkedIn .

articles.snippet: Blue J Announces $176M in Funding at $700M Valuation to Scale AI Tax Research Agent AI Insider

Business & Markets
Blue J Announces $176M in Funding at $700M Valuation to Scale AI Tax Research Agent
By James Dargan · 12 November 2026 · 1 min read
Toronto-based Blue J, which builds AI software for tax research, has secured US$176 million in a round led by Baltimore’s JMI Equity, valuing the company at US$700 million. Existing investors Oak HC/FT, Sapphire Ventures and Intrepid Growth Partners also took part.
Nearly US$100 million will go towards buying shares from employees and early investors, with the remaining US$80 million funding the commercialisation of Blue J’s new agent product and expansion into the UK, its third market after the US and Canada.
Founded in 2015 by University of Toronto law professor Benjamin Alarie and two colleagues, Blue J answers complex tax questions in seconds with source citations. Alarie rebuilt the product around large language models after ChatGPT arrived in 2022, and says accuracy has risen from roughly 50% in early versions to more than 95%.
The deal comes just over a year after a US$122 million round in August 2025. Recurring revenue has since grown 165% to the mid-eight-figure range, and client firms have increased from fewer than 100 three years ago to more than 6,500.
JMI principal Jack Duane said the firm had tracked Blue J for years, heard strongly positive customer feedback and considers the product extremely difficult to replicate thanks to its proprietary data and domain expertise.

Zacua Ventures Raises $135 Million to Invest in AI, Robotics and Industrial Technology
Published on: 11 November، 2026
Zacua Ventures
Zacua Ventures closes its $135 million Fund II to back Physical AI, construction robotics, industrial technology, energy, manufacturing and infrastructure startups.
The next major opportunity in artificial intelligence may not be confined to software applications or foundation models.
Increasingly, investors are looking toward technologies that can transform the physical economy, from construction sites and cement factories to energy networks, manufacturing facilities and data centers.
Zacua Ventures is positioning itself at the center of this shift, closing its second fund at $135 million to expand investments beyond construction technology into a broader range of Physical Industries, including robotics, manufacturing, energy, mining and critical infrastructure.
$135 Million to Back Technologies Building the Physical Economy
Zacua Ventures closed Fund II at $135 million, more than doubling its $56 million debut fund and exceeding its fundraising target by 35%.
The raise reflects growing investor interest in technology applied to capital-intensive industries that have historically attracted less venture capital than software and digital platforms.
The firm’s investment thesis is built around a simple premise: construction, energy, manufacturing and mining are not merely facing productivity challenges.
They need fundamental operational transformation through AI, robotics, data and advanced technologies.
AI Is Moving From Digital Applications to Physical Industries
Zacua’s strategy extends beyond conventional AI tools, targeting companies that deploy technology directly into industrial and field operations.
Its investments include autonomous construction robots, AI platforms that identify project risks before construction begins, and technologies designed to reduce emissions from cement production.
These businesses are becoming increasingly relevant as industries face labor shortages, aging workforces, complex operational processes and growing demand for AI infrastructure.
The opportunity is not simply to automate existing workflows, but to redesign how physical industries operate.
Why Venture Capital Is Turning Toward Physical Industries
Construction, energy, manufacturing and mining represent enormous markets with persistent productivity gaps and substantial infrastructure requirements.
McKinsey estimates that global infrastructure investment needs will reach $106 trillion through 2040, while Gartner projects data-center power demand could reach 290 gigawatts by 2030.
These requirements create opportunities for startups developing technologies that improve industrial productivity, reduce operating costs and reshape supply chains.
However, investing in physical industries is fundamentally different from funding software companies. Technologies must be tested in real operating environments, integrated into existing equipment and workflows, and demonstrate measurable economic value before they can scale.
From Construction Robotics to Low-Carbon Cement
Zacua’s early Fund II investments illustrate the breadth of its strategy.

articles.title: Mavria raises $130 million for factory-built AI data centers
articles.snippet: Mavria raises $130 million for factory-built AI data centers ET Datacenters
articles.text:
AI & Compute Infrastructure
1 min Read
Mavria raises $130 million for factory-built AI data centers
Mavria, an artificial intelligence industrial infrastructure company, has secured US$130 million across pre-seed and seed funding rounds. The company aims to construct data centers and related infrastructure across the United States. Its latest funding round values Mavria at US$1 billion.

Published On Nov 11, 2026 at 11:15 AM IST

Highlights
Mavria secured US$130 million in pre-seed and seed funding rounds.
The company's latest funding round values it at US$1 billion.
Funding will support factory-built AI data center construction in the US.
Mavria aims to standardize manufacturing for accelerated infrastructure deployment.
Mavria , a developer of industrial infrastructure for artificial intelligence, has raised US$130 million through pre-seed and seed funding rounds. This capital will support the construction of data centers and related infrastructure across the United States.
The company's latest funding round values it at US$1 billion. Paradigm led this round, with participation from AMP PBC, Liquid 2, Critical Frontier, and Dream Ventures. Mavria plans to use the funding to secure critical supply chains, expand manufacturing capacity , and grow its workforce, according to a company announcement.
Mavria was founded by former colleagues from the U.S. Department of Energy. Co-founders Nick Poradek and Adam Blake previously served as senior advisors to the U.S. Secretary of Energy, while Co-founder Seth Cohen was a former head of nuclear law and policy.
Adam Blake, Mavria's CEO, noted that the race in intelligence is moving from the lab into the physical world. He stated that intelligence needs data centers, which require power, factories, equipment, supply chains, and skilled workers. Blake highlighted that much of this infrastructure is currently built one custom project at a time, with timelines measured in years.
Mavria's approach focuses on producing infrastructure through standardized manufacturing. This aims to move away from individually designed construction projects, which can be time-consuming. The company's launch coincides with increasing demand for electricity, data centers, and industrial equipment due to the expansion of AI computing capacity. Mavria intends to apply its standardized manufacturing model to a broader range of infrastructure projects beyond its initial focus on data centers.

Imprint Raises $130 Million to Help Brands Build Customer Loyalty as AI Reshapes Commerce
Fundraising News
12.11.2026 10:22 am
Imprint, the payments, loyalty, and customer intelligence platform brands use to make every transaction more valuable, has raised $130 million in new financing, valuing the company at approximately $1.9 billion. The round was led by existing investor Khosla Ventures, with participation from existing investors Hedosophia, Ribbit Capital, Spice, Thrive Capital, and new investor Positive Sum. The funding will support the company’s expansion into new payment options and AI capabilities that help brands recognize and reward customers wherever and however they choose to pay.
Imprint now serves more than two million members and partners with brands representing more than $500 billion in annual U.S. consumer spending. Since the beginning of the year, Imprint has launched programs with Albertsons Companies, Fanatics, Kroger, and Shell, with the Fanatics program debuting this week. Across Imprint’s partner portfolio, total cardholder spending more than doubled between 2025 and 2026. The share of spending on Imprint cards at partner checkouts tripled over the past year. Imprint also recently added $1.5 billion in incremental warehouse capacity and priced its second AAA-rated asset-backed securitization, with investor demand nearly five times the offering size.
As AI changes how people discover, compare, and buy, brands face new challenges in maintaining direct customer relationships. Agentic commerce is projected to mediate up to $1 trillion in U.S. retail revenue by 2030. Imprint brings payments, loyalty, and customer intelligence together so brands can learn from everyday spending and deliver recognition and rewards that give customers reasons to return.
“From AI chats to personal agents, every digital touchpoint is quickly becoming personalized. In this future, the brands that invest in understanding who their customers really are, and building relationships with each individually, will win,” said Daragh Murphy, founder and CEO of Imprint. “Imprint helps brands create financial products to earn a place in their customers’ everyday lives, and make them feel like a regular, uniquely recognizing and rewarding them for their loyalty. The latest round supports our growth as we build more ways for brands to meet customers where they are, regardless of how they want to shop or pay.”

articles.title: Addex Spin-out Neurosterix Closes $105 Million Series B Financing
articles.snippet: Addex Spin-out Neurosterix Closes $105 Million Series B Financing GlobeNewswire
articles.text:
Ad Hoc Announcement Pursuant to Art. 53 LR
Geneva, Switzerland, November 11, 2026 - Addex Therapeutics (SIX and Nasdaq: ADXN), a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on developing a portfolio of novel small molecule allosteric modulators for neurological disorders, today announced that its spin-out company, Neurosterix, has closed a $105 million Series B financing from a syndicate of leading life science investors. Addex did not participate in the financing and its equity interest now represents 8.5% of the issued capital at a valuation of $18.6 million.
The proceeds raised will support mainly the planned Phase 2 clinical development of NTX-253, a highly selective muscarinic M4 positive allosteric modulator (PAM), for schizophrenia. The financing will also support Neurosterix’s broader pipeline of selective allosteric modulators for a range of neuropsychiatric disorders.
“The closing of this significant financing is a huge endorsement of the allosteric approach pioneered by Addex in schizophrenia as well as other neuropsychiatric disorders. Congatulations to the whole Neurosterix team, which has made enormous strides in advancing lead program NTX-253 through clinical development and ready for Phase 2, following our spin-out in 2024,” said Tim Dyer, CEO of Addex.
About NTX-253 and M4 PAMs
The M4 muscarinic receptor is a validated target for treating schizophrenia and related disorders through indirect modulation of dopamine signaling. NTX-253 is a potent, highly selective, oral PAM of M4 that fine-tunes muscarinic signaling in the brain to potentially reduce psychosis symptoms while avoiding the movement disorders and metabolic complications associated with traditional dopamine antagonists. Neurosterix has completed Phase 1 single- and multiple-ascending-dose clinical studies of NTX-253, which data supporting advancing into larger scale Phase 2 clinical studies.
About Neurosterix
Neurosterix is a clinical-stage biotechnology company focused on transforming neuropsychiatric care through selective allosteric modulation. The company’s approach is designed to fine-tune brain signaling with greater precision and selectivity, with the goal of developing safer, more effective treatments for people living with schizophrenia, and mood and anxiety disorders. Neurosterix’s pipeline includes NTX-253, a selective muscarinic M4 positive allosteric modulator (PAM) for schizophrenia; NTX-819, a potentially first-in-class mGlu7 negative allosteric modulator (NAM) for mood and anxiety disorders; and NTX-529, a second differentiated M4 PAM for additional psychosis- and mood-related disorders. Neurosterix has operations in Boston and Geneva. For more information, visit www.neurosterix.com.
About Addex Therapeutics
Addex Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on developing a portfolio of novel small molecule allosteric modulators for neurological disorders. Addex's lead drug candidate, dipraglurant (mGlu5 negative allosteric modulator or NAM), is under evaluation for future development in brain injury recovery, including post-stroke and traumatic brain injury recovery. Addex has selected a GABAB PAM drug candidate for development in substance use disorders and has successfully completed IND enabling studies. In addition, Addex is advancing a differentiated GABAB PAM compound for the treatment of chronic cough.
